svg.title: Power BI Consumption over Semantic Models
svg.desc: An end-to-end architecture diagram showing how governed Fabric data sources flow through Import, DirectQuery, and Direct Lake into a centralized shared semantic model, powering governed Power BI reports and organizational apps.
svg.text: Power BI Consumption & Governance over Semantic Models
Curated Sources ➔ Multi-Mode Ingestion ➔ Centralized Shared Semantic Model ➔ Governed Reports & Apps

g.title: Governed sources — Warehouse, lakehouse, databases, and external systems provide modeled data.
g.text: 1. Governed Data Sources (OneLake, Lakehouses, Warehouses & Databases)
Curated enterprise storage tiers serving raw, conformed, and aggregated data across the tenant
Fabric Lakehouse
Delta Parquet in OneLake
Fabric Warehouse
Relational T-SQL Endpoint
Fabric SQL Database
Autonomous Operational DB
External & On-Premises
Cloud / On-Prem Gateway Sources

g.title: Import mode — Import copies a snapshot into model memory and refreshes it.
g.text: 2. IMPORT (VERTIPAQ IN-MEMORY)
In-Memory Compressed Cache
• Sub-second visual response times
• 10x dictionary compression in VertiPaq engine
• Full DAX & Power Query transformation support
Operational Characteristics:
• Freshness: Point-in-time snapshot refreshed on schedule
• Concurrency: Highly elastic capacity scaling for heavy user loads
• Large Model Format: Removes 1 GB ceiling up to SKU limit
• Gateway: Required for on-prem DBs without direct IP routing
Standard: Best for executive dashboards & dimension tables
Watch-outs & Refresh Costs:
❌ Data duplication into Power BI memory space
❌ Lengthy refresh processing times on large multi-GB facts
❌ Peak refresh memory consumption can trigger capacity throttling
Avoid for multi-billion row tables where Direct Lake applies.

g.title: DirectQuery mode — DirectQuery delegates report queries to the source.
g.text: 3. DIRECTQUERY (LIVE DELEGATION)
Zero-Storage Query Pushdown
• Translates visual DAX to native SQL on the fly
• Results always reflect 100% current source state
• Eliminates scheduled data refresh wait cycles
Operational Characteristics:
• Freshness: Real-time (live queries on visual rendering)
• Security: Evaluates source database user permissions directly
• Auditability: Meets strict data residency & compliance mandates
• Return Limits: 1,000,000 row query limit enforced
Standard: Best for operational real-time monitoring
Watch-outs & Latency Costs:
❌ Slower visual render times (dependent on source DB health)
❌ Report clicks generate heavy concurrent query load on source
❌ DAX limitations: Complex calculations fail to fold to SQL
Requires query reduction and source indexing.

g.title: Direct Lake mode — Direct Lake reads eligible Delta from OneLake and caches hot data.
g.text: 4. DIRECT LAKE (ONELAKE ZERO-COPY)
Direct OneLake Delta Lake Access
• VertiPaq query speed with ZERO data copy
• Lazy on-demand column paging on query touch
• Seconds-scale metadata framing keeps data fresh
Operational Characteristics:
• Freshness: Current as of latest metadata framing event
• Memory Paging: Only queried columns are transcoded & cached
• Scale: Seamlessly queries hundreds of millions of rows
• Flavors: OneLake API native vs SQL Endpoint mediated
Standard: The flagship storage mode for Microsoft Fabric
Key Governance Guardrails:
• Direct Lake on OneLake cannot fall back to DirectQuery
• Direct Lake on SQL falls back if table is based on a SQL view
• Guardrails: Delta tables must stay within SKU memory limits
Always build Direct Lake models on base Delta tables!

g.title: Shared semantic model — The model centralizes relationships, measures, and report security.
g.text: 5. Centralized Shared Semantic Model
Single governed business contract powering multi-report consumption
Business Measures
Centralized DAX logic
Security Governance
Row & Object level RLS
Endorsement
Promoted / Certified
• Decouples data model engineering from report authoring and visual design
• Eliminates duplicated metric definitions and contradictory reporting numbers
Hub-and-Spoke Semantic Architecture:
• Upstream data engineers own the semantic model in a dedicated core workspace.
• Report authors across lines of business build self-service reports using Live Connect.
• Build permissions control access while preventing schema tampering.
Standard: 1 Core Semantic Model ➔ Many Downstream Reports!

g.title: Reports and apps — Reports analyze one model; apps package content for audiences.
g.text: 6. Governed Distribution: Power BI Reports & Apps
Audience-tailored delivery packaged for enterprise business consumers
Power BI Apps
Packaged distribution
Interactive Reports
Drill-down analytics
Live Excel & APIs
Pivot tables & REST
• Multiple distinct reports bind to the same underlying shared semantic model
• Power BI Apps package reports, dashboards, and workbooks into a single secure URL
Audience Management & Security Boundary:
• Use App Audiences to partition executive, management, and operational views.
• Consumers receive read-only app access without workspace membership.
• Protects workspace items from unauthorized accidental edits or deletions.
Enterprise Standard: Distribute to consumers exclusively via Power BI Apps!
